title: December Pacific SST gave an uncertain spring North Atlantic forecast gain in a 1981-2025 ERSSTv5 test
abstract: We tested whether December sea surface temperature in the Nino 3.4 region adds spring forecast information for the tropical North Atlantic. We used NOAA ERSSTv5 and 45 March-May targets from 1981 to 2025. Each fit used earlier target years only. Adding Pacific temperature to local December temperature and a linear year term reduced mean squared error by 24.6%. RMSE fell from 0.444 to 0.385 C. The conditional 95% five-year block interval for error reduction was -13.6% to 47.6%. Rolling 30-year fits and a local November control gave positive point gains with intervals that included zero. The known Pacific-Atlantic link thus gave an uncertain added forecast benefit in this test. One revised SST product, a short test record, model choices and conditional intervals limit inference. This result does not establish an operational gain or a physical cause. Code, aggregate inputs, every forecast, source hashes, checks and a figure are included.

display.caption: Added Pacific temperature forecast gains and cumulative saved squared error. The 95% intervals use paired five-year blocks and hold fitted forecasts fixed.
